title: Samsung Philippines names the top 10 changemakers of Solve for Tomorrow 2026
summary: The results are in – Samsung unveils the finalists of Solve for Tomorrow 2026 in the Philippines, the annual student competition under its global program, putting the spotlight on young Filipino…

blocks.text: The results are in – Samsung unveils the finalists of Solve for Tomorrow 2026 in the Philippines, the annual student competition under its global program, putting the spotlight on young Filipino changemakers ready to make a difference.
The top 10 teams that will move forward in the competition are:

items: Team SAGIP from Quezon City Science High School;
Team CheckMite from Siaton Science High School;
Ligtas Skwela from Philippine Science High School Caraga Region Campus;
Team HydroHero from Valenzuela City School of Mathematics and Science;
From Pulp to Brine from Lanao Del Norte Provincial Science and Technology;
Team KINAIYAHAN from Bayawan City Science and Technology Education Center High School;
Team KUHOL-LECTOR from Philippine Science High School Main;
Team AgriSpectra from Eastern Visayas Regional Science High School;
Team VoltROOT from Tagbilaran City Science High School; and
Team CanalCare from Baguio City National Science High School.

blocks.text: As part of Samsung’s global commitment to youth tech education, Solve for Tomorrow provides students with a platform to turn their ideas into real-world solutions in partnership with the Department of Education. The initiative encourages students in Grades 8 to 10 from government-managed science high schools nationwide to develop innovative, STEM-driven solutions that address challenges in their own communities. Top 10 finalists will vie to be among the three grand winners, who will receive almost PHP 2 million in total of cash prizes and Samsung devices for their schools, teams, and teacher advisers.

For 2026, Samsung received over 500 submissions, involving more than 1000 students from all 15 regions in the country. Each team, composed of up to four student members, was challenged to develop a proposal inspired by one of three themes: Environmental Sustainability through Technology, Social Change through Tech and Sport, and Solving Community Problems with Artificial Intelligence (AI).

Samsung also brought together a distinguished panel of industry leaders from the fields of technology, innovation, and education to serve as judges – Alwyn Rosel, Executive Director of QBO Innovation; Ria Liza Canlas, President of the Filipino Women Inventors Society; Jaton Zulueta, Executive Director and Founder of AHA Learning Center; Grahssel Dungca, Luzon Programs Co-Lead of DEVCON Philippines; and Jun Guevara, Head of Corporate Marketing at Samsung Electronics Philippines.
The 10 finalists will also be mentored by Samsung experts to refine proposals and build proof-of-concepts ahead of the final presentation.

“It’s inspiring to see more students from different communities take part and share their ideas for a better future. Witnessing their unique perspective on local community challenges and their drive to pioneer solutions show just how much potential young Filipinos have. We’re proud to be part of their journey and excited to see where it will take them as they move forward in the competition,” shared Roman Han, President of Samsung Electronics Philippines.
